Using the formula for the average rate of change, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{Δf}{Δx} & =\frac{f(b)-f(a)}{b-a} \\  & =\frac{f(3)-f(-2)}{3-(-2)} \\  & =\frac{(p+10)-(2p-1)}{3+2} \\  & =\frac{11-p}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we know that $\frac{Δf}{Δx}=3$ on the interval $[-2,3].$ Thus, 

$$
\frac{11-p}{5}=3.
$$

Solving for $p,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{11-p}{5} & =3 \\ 11-p & =15 \\ -p & =15-11 \\ -p & =4 \\ p & =-4.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.worked_solution:
We have $\frac{Δf}{Δx}=0$ if and only if $Δf=0.$ So

$$
\begin{aligned} & Δf=0 \\  & f(b)-f(a)=0 \\  & f(b)=f(a).\end{aligned}
$$

This means we have to find an interval  $[a,b]$ such that $f(a)=f(b).$

Since $f(8)=f(14)=6,$ we conclude that $\frac{Δf}{Δx}=0$ on the interval $[8,14].$
